title_en: Exclusive Economic Zone and Continental Shelf Act of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted to protect the sovereign rights and jurisdiction of the People's Republic of China over its exclusive economic zone and continental shelf, and to safeguard the national maritime rights and interests.

Article 2 The exclusive economic zone of the People's Republic of China means the area beyond and adjacent to the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China, extending to 200 nautical miles from the baselines from which the breadth of the territorial sea is measured. The continental shelf of the People's Republic of China means the seabed and subsoil of the submarine area that extends throughout the natural prolongation of its land territory beyond the territorial sea to the outer edge of the continental margin; if the distance from the baselines from which the breadth of the territorial sea is measured to the outer edge of the continental margin is less than 200 nautical miles, it extends to 200 nautical miles. Where the claims of the People's Republic of China regarding the exclusive economic zone and the continental shelf overlap with those of an adjacent or opposite state, the delimitation shall be effected by agreement on the basis of international law and in accordance with the principle of fairness.

Article 3 The People's Republic of China exercises sovereign rights in the exclusive economic zone for the purpose of exploring, exploiting, conserving and managing the natural resources of the waters superjacent to the seabed and of the seabed and its subsoil, and for the purpose of carrying out other economic activities for the exploitation and exploration of the zone, such as the production of energy from the water, currents and winds. The People's Republic of China exercises jurisdiction over the establishment and use of artificial islands, installations and structures in the exclusive economic zone, marine scientific research, and the protection and preservation of the marine environment. For the purposes of this Law, the natural resources of the exclusive economic zone include living and non-living resources.

Article 4 The People's Republic of China exercises sovereign rights over the continental shelf for the purpose of exploring the continental shelf and exploiting its natural resources. The People's Republic of China exercises jurisdiction over the establishment and use of artificial islands, installations and structures on the continental shelf, marine scientific research, and the protection and preservation of the marine environment. The People's Republic of China has the exclusive right to authorize and regulate drilling on the continental shelf for all purposes. For the purposes of this Law, the natural resources of the continental shelf include the mineral and other non-living resources of the seabed and subsoil, and living organisms belonging to sedentary species, that is to say, organisms which, at the harvestable stage, either are immobile on or under the seabed or are unable to move except in constant physical contact with the seabed or subsoil.

Article 5 Any international organization, foreign organization or individual must, upon approval by the competent authorities of the People's Republic of China, enter the exclusive economic zone of the People's Republic of China for fishing activities and shall abide by the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China and the treaties and agreements concluded between the People's Republic of China and the relevant states. The competent authorities of the People's Republic of China have the right to take various necessary conservation and management measures to ensure that living resources in the exclusive economic zone are not endangered by over-exploitation.

Article 6 The competent authorities of the People's Republic of China have the right to conserve and manage straddling stocks, highly migratory species, marine mammals, anadromous stocks originating in the rivers of the People's Republic of China, and catadromous species which spend the greater part of their life cycle in the waters of the People's Republic of China. The People's Republic of China has the primary interest in anadromous stocks originating in its rivers.

Article 7 Any international organization, foreign organization or individual must, upon approval by the competent authorities of the People's Republic of China, carry out activities for the exploration and exploitation of natural resources in the exclusive economic zone and continental shelf of the People's Republic of China or engage in drilling on the continental shelf of the People's Republic of China for any purpose, and shall abide by the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China.

Article 8 The People's Republic of China has the exclusive right to construct and to authorize and regulate the construction, operation and use of artificial islands, installations and structures in the exclusive economic zone and on the continental shelf. The People's Republic of China exercises exclusive jurisdiction over artificial islands, installations and structures in the exclusive economic zone and on the continental shelf, including jurisdiction with regard to customs, fiscal, health, safety and immigration laws and regulations. The competent authorities of the People's Republic of China have the right to establish safety zones around artificial islands, installations and structures in the exclusive economic zone and on the continental shelf and may take appropriate measures in such zones to ensure the safety of navigation and the safety of the artificial islands, installations and structures.

Article 9 Any international organization, foreign organization or individual must, upon approval by the competent authorities of the People's Republic of China, conduct marine scientific research in the exclusive economic zone and on the continental shelf of the People's Republic of China, and shall abide by the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China.

Article 10 The competent authorities of the People's Republic of China have the right to take necessary measures to prevent, reduce and control pollution of the marine environment and to protect and preserve the marine environment of the exclusive economic zone and the continental shelf.

Article 11 Any state, subject to compliance with international law and the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China, enjoys the freedom of navigation and overflight in the exclusive economic zone of the People's Republic of China, and the freedom to lay submarine cables and pipelines in the exclusive economic zone and on the continental shelf of the People's Republic of China, as well as other lawful uses of the sea related to such freedoms. The course for laying submarine cables and pipelines must be agreed to by the competent authorities of the People's Republic of China.

Article 12 When exercising its sovereign rights for the purpose of exploring, exploiting, conserving and managing living resources in the exclusive economic zone, the People's Republic of China may take such necessary measures as boarding, inspection, arrest, detention and judicial proceedings to ensure compliance with the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China. The People's Republic of China has the right to take necessary measures, investigate legal liability according to law, and may exercise the right of hot pursuit in respect of any act in the exclusive economic zone or on the continental shelf that violates the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China.

Article 13 Rights enjoyed by the People's Republic of China over the exclusive economic zone and the continental shelf not provided for in this Law shall be exercised in accordance with international law and other relevant laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China.
Article 14 The provisions of this Law shall not affect the historic rights enjoyed by the People's Republic of China.
Article 15 The State Council of the People's Republic of China may formulate relevant provisions in accordance with this Law.
Article 16 This Law shall come into force on the date of its promulgation.
